quizzes.title: Module 1 — Tuesday — Building Your First Edit
quizzes.description: Tuesday's quiz covers cutting and trimming, splitting clips, rearranging your timeline, using transitions, adding text, working with music, export settings, and changing aspect ratio from landscape to portrait.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of cutting and trimming footage?
options: To increase the video's resolution
To keep the useful parts of a clip and remove unnecessary sections
To automatically add music to the video
To change a landscape video into portrait
questions.explanation: Cutting and trimming is about selection — keeping what serves the edit and removing what does not.

questions.prompt: What does splitting a clip allow an editor to do?
options: Turn a video clip into an audio file
Increase the frame rate of the clip
Divide one clip into separate sections that can be edited independently
Export multiple videos at once
questions.explanation: Splitting breaks one clip into parts so each can be moved, trimmed or removed on its own.

questions.prompt: Why is rearranging clips important when building a video?
options: The order of clips can affect the flow, meaning, and story of the video
It automatically improves the quality of every clip
It removes the need to trim footage
It changes the video's aspect ratio
questions.explanation: Order is meaning. The same shots in a different sequence can tell a different story or change how the viewer feels.

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the proper use of transitions?
options: Every clip should have a different transition
Transitions should be used as frequently as possible
Transitions should replace good editing decisions
Transitions should serve the edit rather than distract from it
questions.explanation: A transition should support what the edit is doing. If it draws attention to itself, it is working against the video.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a common use of text in video content?
options: Increasing the video's frame rate
Creating subtitles, titles, labels, or announcements
Removing unwanted footage
Changing the video's file format
questions.explanation: Text carries information the visuals cannot — subtitles, titles, labels and announcements.

questions.prompt: How can music contribute to a video?
options: It can support the pacing, mood, and overall viewing experience
It automatically fixes poorly edited footage
It changes the video's aspect ratio
It removes the need for visual content
questions.explanation: Music shapes pace and feeling. It cannot rescue an edit that was not made well in the first place.

They are only needed when adding text
They help ensure the finished video is saved with appropriate settings for its intended use
They automatically remove unwanted footage
questions.explanation: Export settings decide what the finished file actually is — resolution, frame rate and format — so the video works where you intend to publish it.

questions.prompt: You created a video in landscape format, but you want to publish it as a portrait video for a platform that uses vertical content. What should you do?
options: Split every clip in the timeline
Change the project's aspect ratio from landscape to portrait and adjust the framing as needed
Add a transition between every clip
Increase the video's frame rate
questions.explanation: Change the project's aspect ratio and then reframe each shot, so the important parts of the image stay visible in the new shape.
